compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Epic fattish-plucky-bufflehead (62dc-535b-5d05-421d) needs a retrieval architecture chosen on measurement, not on the July N = 8 experiment. The store already holds a labeled set: 51 known duplicate pairs identified in ticket exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish (eac3), of which 44 are semantic. This story builds that benchmark from the store, measures three candidate architectures against it, and records the decision as an ADR.

## Approach

Build a benchmark spec from the 51 pairs exactly as ticket eac3 did: collect every recorded `duplicates` link across the store (`rebar list --full` and read each ticket's `deps` for the `duplicates` relation; the relation vocabulary is in `docs/ticket-model.md`), close the links transitively into clusters, and enumerate the pairs within each cluster, storing pair ids and the title plus first 2,000 characters of description per ticket as a committed JSON fixture under `evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json`. Measure recall@5 and recall@10 for each candidate with the same query text (title plus first 200 characters of description, the compose-time shape):

1. Lexical baseline: SQLite FTS5 with `bm25()` over title (weight 5.0) and description (weight 1.0) in a temporary index built from the fixture.
2. Digest lexical: BM25F over LLM digests produced with the retired `ticket_digest` prompt at the commit before its removal (recorded on the closing comment of the removal story under epic bossy-skittish-foal), trivial model class, one call per ticket, cached in the fixture directory keyed by content hash.
3. Vector: embeddings of an LLM summary (the same digest text joined as one paragraph) from Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, model id `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, called with the boto3 `bedrock-runtime` client's `invoke_model` and a JSON body of `{"inputText": ..., "dimensions": 1024, "normalize": true}` (model card: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-titan-text-embeddings-v2.html; input limit 8,192 tokens / 50,000 characters, so the summary is truncated to 40,000 characters before the call), region from `rebar.toml` `[llm] bedrock_region_name`, boto3 provided by the `bedrock` extra (`pyproject.toml` `[project.optional-dependencies] bedrock`), cosine similarity by brute force over the fixture (5k normalized vectors need no ANN library).

Write the ADR (next free number per `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`) recording the three recall tables, the chosen architecture, the index location (`<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`, keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch), the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>` on the tickets branch), and the cost model (summarization and embedding calls per changed ticket).

## Scope

- `evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json` (new), `evals/similar-tickets/measure.py` (new; the runner for the three candidates), `evals/similar-tickets/README.md` (new). The top-level `evals/` tree is created by the eval-harness epic's corpus-move story; this story depends on it.
- `docs/adr/0NNN-similar-ticket-retrieval.md` (new).
- `docs/adr/README.md` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`).

## Testing

- Happy path: `python evals/similar-tickets/measure.py --candidate fts5` prints a recall table for 51 queries; the fixture loads and every pair resolves to two existing ticket ids.
- Edge: a pair whose ticket has an empty description still yields a query from the title alone; the runner skips a candidate cleanly when the Bedrock credentials are absent and says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json` holds 51 pairs with ids, aliases, titles, and description heads, and `measure.py --check` validates every id resolves in the store. Checked by running the command.
- [ ] Recall@5 and recall@10 are recorded for all three candidates in the ADR, produced by `measure.py` with the exact command lines quoted. Checked by re-running each command and matching the ADR table.
- [ ] The ADR names one architecture, its index path, freshness key, catch-up rule, embedding model, and per-ticket cost, and is indexed in `docs/adr/README.md`. Checked by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` and `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`.
